purpose: Offline NeuFlow v2 export+validation runtime for models/export_neuflow_v2.py. CPU-only and device-independent: like bakeoff/waft-validation and unlike bakeoff/p25-6/runtime-inputs.json this runtime carries NO ONNX Runtime CUDA-12 archive and NO native ORT bridge -- onnxruntime is the exact CPU wheel pip-installed at CI build (onnxruntime==1.16.3), because conda-forge does not carry a satisfiable 1.16.3 for this stack. Python is 3.9 to match the NeuFlow v2 validated export environment recorded in models/neuflow-v2.json (export_environment.python 3.9.6); the pinned upstream README's python==3.8 is EOL and no longer conda-forge-built. UNLIKE bakeoff/waft-validation it also carries NO vendored upstream source: NeuFlow v2's checkpoints are 36MB real git blobs tracked IN the upstream repo, so a clean vendored checkout cannot exclude the unknown-licence checkpoint without dirtying the worktree export_neuflow_v2.py requires clean. The operator therefore supplies their own clean NeuFlow_v2 checkout (which inherently contains neuflow_mixed.pth) plus the verified checkpoint; the pack carries only the runtime, entrypoint closure, manifest and instructions.

conda.note: explicit_lock is the REQUESTED match-spec (not @EXPLICIT); explicit_lock_sha256 is the SHA256 of THAT checked-in requested spec and CI's preflight validates it against the requested file, so it must ALWAYS track conda-el8-x86_64.lock -- never overwrite it with a solved digest. CI solves the spec on EL8 x86_64 and emits the pinned @EXPLICIT lock as evidence (conda list --explicit -> whitewater-neuflow-validation-runtime.inventory). solved_lock_sha256 records the SHA256 of THAT emitted @EXPLICIT lock: leave it "" until the first qualifying solve, read the digest CI prints, and set it here (distinct from explicit_lock_sha256) to pin the reproducible solve for the qualifying re-dispatch. When set non-empty, CI validates the emitted @EXPLICIT lock against it and fails closed on drift; when "", CI only emits it for review. ORT SOURCING: onnxruntime is NOT in the requested spec (conda-forge does not carry 1.16.3). CI pip-installs the exact CPU wheel onnxruntime==1.16.3 into the solved env AFTER the conda solve and BEFORE conda-pack and the runtime-license inventory, so it is packed into the runtime and reported by licenses.py as a pip identity (pip://onnxruntime==1.16.3) for the licence-supplement population step. PYTHON: the spec pins python 3.9 (matching models/neuflow-v2.json export_environment.python 3.9.6, the validated export interpreter), not the README's EOL 3.8.

export_dependencies.note: The numeric export stack mirrors models/requirements-neuflow-export.txt (pytorch==2.0.1, torchvision==0.15.2, numpy==1.24.4, onnx==1.14.1, onnxruntime==1.16.3); python is 3.9 (models/neuflow-v2.json validated export interpreter) rather than the README's EOL 3.8. torch/numpy/onnx are conda specs; onnxruntime is pip-installed at CI build (conda-forge lacks 1.16.3). These are REQUESTED versions; the CI-solved @EXPLICIT lock is the reproducible identity. NeuFlow's model construction imports only torch and huggingface_hub (the latter stubbed inert by export_neuflow_v2.py), so -- unlike WAFT which needed einops -- there is no scipy/safetensors/timm/einops dependency to add.
export_dependencies.torchvision: 0.15.2 (cpu build variant; carried for stack parity, not imported by the NeuFlow model/export path)
export_dependencies.onnxruntime: 1.16.3 (pip-installed CPU wheel at CI build, not conda-sourced; CPUExecutionProvider only)

python38_torch201_risk.pinned: python 3.9 (conda) + pytorch 2.0.1 (cpu, conda) + numpy 1.24.4 (conda) + onnx 1.14.1 (conda) + onnxruntime 1.16.3 (pip-installed CPU wheel at CI build)
python38_torch201_risk.reason: RESOLVED the original python-3.8 EOL blocker: the first EL8 solve confirmed python 3.8 is unsatisfiable on conda-forge (it stopped building new py38 packages after upstream EOL 2024-10), so the spec now pins python 3.9 -- which is both conda-forge-built AND the NeuFlow v2 validated export interpreter recorded in models/neuflow-v2.json (export_environment.python 3.9.6), so the linux re-export runs on the exact framework the frozen validation.* thresholds were produced on. onnxruntime 1.16.3 is also not on conda-forge, so it is pip-installed as the exact CPU wheel after the conda solve rather than solved. torch 2.0.1 / numpy 1.24.4 / onnx 1.14.1 predate conda-forge's py38 drop and are co-installable on py39; the residual risk is only that these co-resolve on py39 for linux-64, which CI's EL8 solve proves.
python38_torch201_risk.remediation: If the EL8 solve fails closed on an unsatisfiable py39 graph, do NOT hand-pin build hashes here. First try raising only Python to the lowest conda-forge-built version that still carries torch 2.0.1 (updating conda-el8-x86_64.lock in step), re-solve, and re-run the weightless NeuFlow construction smoke (the checkpoint's strict load is the on-box proof the framework still matches the tensors). If the pip onnxruntime==1.16.3 wheel is unavailable for the chosen Python, pick the nearest wheel matching models/neuflow-v2.json export_environment.runtime in review. If torch 2.0.1 is not co-installable with any conda-forge-built Python, escalate the framework bump to Andrew rather than silently drifting the numeric stack the manifest thresholds were frozen against; then recompute conda.explicit_lock_sha256 for the edited requested spec and, after the re-solve, set conda.solved_lock_sha256 to the newly emitted @EXPLICIT lock digest before re-dispatching.

neuflow_source.note: export_neuflow_v2.py verifies source identity with `git rev-parse HEAD` and a clean-worktree check, so --upstream must be a clean git checkout at the pinned commit. UNLIKE bakeoff/waft-validation, this pack does NOT vendor that checkout: NeuFlow v2 tracks its checkpoints (neuflow_mixed.pth, neuflow_sintel.pth, neuflow_things.pth -- 36MB real git blobs each, NOT git-lfs pointers; the repo has no .gitattributes) directly in the source tree, so a clean vendored checkout would redistribute the unknown-licence neuflow_mixed.pth, while stripping the .pth files would dirty the worktree export_neuflow_v2.py refuses (upstream_worktree_dirty). The licence-safe, provable choice is to carry no upstream tree at all. The operator clones NeuFlow_v2 at the pinned commit themselves on a networked machine (that clone inherently contains neuflow_mixed.pth) and brings the clean checkout onto the box on media; CI clones the same commit only to run the weightless construction smoke and never packages it. `git` is resolved from the box's /usr/bin (the airgap wrapper's PATH is runtime/bin:/usr/bin:/bin); it is deliberately NOT bundled (GPLv2).

submodules.reason: NeuFlow_v2 at the pinned commit has NO .gitmodules and no git submodules (verified against the repository tree). There is nothing to exclude for submodule-licence reasons, unlike WAFT's non-commercial thirdparty/dinov3. CI asserts the absence of .gitmodules so a future submodule cannot enter unnoticed.

checkpoint.note: The checkpoint is NEVER downloaded by CI or embedded in the package. It is a tracked file in the pinned upstream repo, so the operator's own clean checkout already contains it; the operator verifies these exact bytes off-box and may point --checkpoint at the in-tree neuflow_mixed.pth or a separately-verified copy. Its file-level licence remains unknown regardless of any numerical validation pass (see models/neuflow-v2.json checkpoint.license and exclusion.reason_code checkpoint_license_terms_unknown); nothing here authorizes redistributing it, which is exactly why the pack carries no upstream tree.
